# slidemachina

> An HTML presentation engine on React. A presentation is one file, `index.tsx`, written in JSX; the theme is `style.css` next to it, pictures are in `images/`. The build is an HTML file, a website, a PDF or PowerPoint.

A reference for agents: everything needed to write, style and check a presentation. The full engine documentation (in Russian) is `docs/slidemachina.md` in https://github.com/xfenix/slidemachina.

## Commands

```bash
npx slidemachina dev [folder]                # slides in the browser; a .tsx change shows up at once, on the same step
npx slidemachina build [folder] --html --pdf # without flags it asks what to build
npx slidemachina check [folder] [--json]     # the rules of a clear talk, see below; exit code 1 when there are remarks
npx slidemachina shot 12 [folder]            # slide 12 as a PNG; 12.2 is after two steps, 12+1 is the first hidden slide after 12
npx slidemachina meme "this is fine"         # meme search; every result is printed with the command that inserts it
```

- `build` flags: `--html` (one file), `--protected` (password from `SLIDEMACHINA_PASSWORD`), `--folder`, `--zip`, `--pdf`, `--steps` (PDF by steps), `--pptx`, `--no-hidden` (PDF and PowerPoint without hidden slides; by default they are in), `--out <folder>`.
- `shot` writes `slide-12.png` to the current folder; `--out file.png` writes elsewhere. Use it to check the layout by eye, not by reading code. PDF, covers and `shot` need Chrome installed.
- Browser address: `#7` is slide 7, `#7.2` is after two steps, `?print` is the print view, `?overview` is the slide overview.

## Files

```text
my-talk/
  index.tsx    the presentation
  style.css    the theme: @import "tailwindcss" and CSS variables
  images/      pictures, imported in index.tsx
```

A repository of talks is a folder with presentations in subfolders and a shared theme `theme/style.css`. A talk's own theme is stronger than the shared one.

## Skeleton

```tsx
import * as Machina from "slidemachina";
import logoPicture from "./images/logo.svg";

export default (
  <Machina.Presentation lang="en" logo={logoPicture}>
    <Machina.Slide cover>
      <h1>My talk</h1>
      <p className="machina-lead">A subtitle</p>
    </Machina.Slide>
    <Machina.Section title="A section">
      <Machina.Slide>
        <h2>The thought of the slide</h2>
        <ul data-steps>
          <li>An item appears on a key press</li>
          <li>The second item</li>
        </ul>
        <Machina.Notes>What to say on this slide</Machina.Notes>
      </Machina.Slide>
    </Machina.Section>
  </Machina.Presentation>
);
```

- `index.tsx` exports a default element. Your own component is declared right in the file, above the slides.
- `Presentation`: `title`, `lang` (`ru`, `en`), `align` (`left`, `center`, `right`), `logo` (a file, `{ light, dark }` or a component), `transition`, `speed`, `stepEffect`, `aspectRatio` (`"16:9"` by default, `"4:3"`, `"9:16"`…), `progress={false}`, `breadcrumbsSeparator`, `typography={false}`, `date` (`"2026-10-30"`), `duration` (minutes of the talk), `favicon`, `onChange`.
- `Section`: `title`; a nested `Section` is a subsection. A section adds its own numbered cover "02". The first `<Slide cover>` of a section replaces that cover; `cover={false}` removes it.
- `Slide`: `cover`, `align`, `valign` (`top`, `center`, `bottom`), `background` (a color, picture, video, GIF or `{ iframe: "https://…" }`), `tone` (`dark`, `light`), `transition`, `speed`, `stepEffect`, `plain` (no logo, breadcrumbs or number), `logo` (`"top-right"`, `"top-left"`, `"top"`, `"center"`, `"bottom"`, `false`), `breadcrumbs`, `number={false}`, `hidden` (skipped on stage, kept in print, PDF and PowerPoint: details for the sent copy, answers to questions), `className`, `onEnter`, `onLeave`.
- A cover has `h1`, a regular slide has `h2`.
- `<Machina.Notes>` are speaker notes, `<Machina.Notes step={2}>` belong to step 2. They are not on the slide; the P key opens the presenter window.
- `useSlide()` in your own component: `{ number, step, isCurrent, isCopy }`.

## Steps

- `data-steps` on `ul`, `ol`, `table` or `machina-columns`: every item, row or column appears on a key press. `data-steps={3}` starts at step 3.
- `data-step` turns any tag into a step, even a `<span>` inside a line. `data-step={2}` puts it on step 2.
- Effects: `rise` (default), `fade`, `scale`, `glitch`, `highlight` (lights up in the accent color), `dim` (fades out). On an element: `data-step-effect="fade"`. For all steps of a presentation or a slide: `stepEffect="fade"`.
- Diagram parts (`step`), code lines (`lines`) and scene objects (`step`) have steps too.

## Blocks

| Markup | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<p className="machina-lead">` | A subtitle or an opening phrase |
| `<p>` | Body text |
| `<p className="machina-note">` | A small note |
| `<p className="machina-source">` | The source of the data, under the blocks |
| `<div className="machina-columns">` | Columns: every direct child is a column. Shares: `style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "3fr 2fr" }}` |
| `<figure className="machina-big-number"><p>42</p><figcaption>…</figcaption></figure>` | A big number with a caption |
| `<div className="machina-card">` | A card; `machina-card-stretch` takes all the free space |
| `<ul className="machina-bars"><li style={{ height: "30%" }} /></ul>` | A bar chart |
| `<table>` with `thead` and `tbody` | A table |
| `<table className="machina-compare">`, `<td className="machina-yes" />`, `<td className="machina-no" />` | A comparison of options with check marks |
| `<figure><blockquote>…</blockquote><figcaption>Author</figcaption></figure>` | A quote |
| `<p className="machina-thesis">` on `<Slide background="var(--accent-soft-color)">` | A thesis: one phrase, large, no heading. A longer phrase is `machina-thesis-small` |
| `<div className="machina-pin machina-pin-bottom machina-pin-right">` | A block on top of the slide, at its edge |
| `<div className="machina-freeform">` | Free layout under the heading, children are `absolute` |
| `<figcaption>` after a block | A caption for a diagram, code, table or scene |

Block components:
- `Image`: `src`, `alt`, `stretch` (fills the free space), `full` (the whole slide), `fit` (`contain`, `cover`), `float` (`left`, `right`: text flows around it); `<figcaption>` inside.
- `Video`: `src`, `poster`, `stretch`, `full`, `fit`, `loop`, `controls`.
- `QR`: `value`, `logo`, `color`, `correction`; `<figcaption>` inside.
- `Meme`: `src`, `alt`, `float`; captions inside, one `<p>` per line, `data-place` (`top`, `bottom`, `center`), and `<figcaption>` with the source.

## Code

```tsx
<Machina.Code lang="ts" title="app.ts">{`const answer = 42;`}</Machina.Code>
<Machina.Code src="./agent.py" lines="10-13 | 27-30" numbers />
```

- `lines="1 | 3-4 | 6"`: the first part shows at once, every next part is a step, the other lines are dimmed.
- `// [!code highlight]` in a comment highlights a line.
- The build does the highlighting, so write code as a string, not a variable.
- One line of code without `title` is shown large and without a background, which suits a command.

## Diagrams

```tsx
<Machina.Diagram direction="right">
  <Machina.Box id="slides">index.tsx<small>slides</small></Machina.Box>
  <Machina.Group id="build" title="Build" step>
    <Machina.Box id="vite">Vite</Machina.Box>
    <Machina.Box id="shiki">Shiki</Machina.Box>
    <Machina.Arrow from="vite" to="shiki" />
  </Machina.Group>
  <Machina.Arrow from="slides" to="vite" label="HTTP" step />
  <Machina.Focus on={["build"]} step />
</Machina.Diagram>
```

- ELK lays out the boxes, no coordinates needed. `column={n}`, `first` and `last` set a box's column.
- `Focus on={[…]}` dims everything else; `<Focus step />` without `on` removes the focus.
- A sequence diagram: `<Machina.Sequence>`, `<Machina.Actor id>`, `<Machina.Message from to label reply step>`, `Focus`.
- A diagram box flows into the box with the same `id` on the next slide.

## 3D

```tsx
<Machina.Scene orbit>
  <Machina.Cube id="cube" size={1.3} material="glossy" />
  <Machina.Sphere size={1} position={[1.5, 0.5, 0]} color="var(--accent-color)" step />
  <Machina.Move on="cube" position={[-1.5, 0.65, 0]} step />
  <Machina.Text position={[0, 2.2, 0]} step>Done</Machina.Text>
</Machina.Scene>
```

- Objects: `id`, `position`, `rotation` (degrees), `scale`, `color`, `material` (`matte`, `glossy`, `metal`), `spin`, `step`.
- `Light`, `Camera` (`position`, `target`, `fov`), `Move` (`on`, `position`, `rotation`, `scale`, `color`). Without `Camera` the frame is chosen automatically. `full` puts the scene under the text on the whole slide.

## Transitions and morphing

- `transition`: `auto` (default), `morph`, `slide`, `fade`, `zoom`, `cube`, `flip`, `wipe`, `iris`, `blinds`, `mosaic`, `glitch`, `none`. `speed`: `fast`, `slow` or a number.
- Morphing finds pairs automatically: equal headings and texts (word by word), pictures with the same `src`, cards, numbers and bars in order, diagram boxes with the same `id`, code line by line. Name your own pair with `morph="name"` on both slides.
- To show a change, repeat the slide with the same heading and change one part.

## Theme

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@font-face {
  font-family: "Brand Sans";
  font-weight: 400 900;
  src: url("./fonts/brand-sans.woff2") format("woff2-variations");
}

:root {
  --font-text: "Brand Sans", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-heading: var(--font-text);
  --heading-weight: 800;
  --accent-color: #e8574c;         /* bullets, numbers, highlights */
  --second-accent-color: #2f7d6d;
  --text-color: #1d1f24;
  --muted-color: #6e6f73;
  --slide-background: #fbfaf7;
  --dark-background: #15161b;
  --section-background: #1d2233;
}

/* Plain CSS changes anything the variables do not cover: it is stronger than the engine's styles. */
[data-slide] :is(h1, h2) { text-transform: uppercase; }
[data-slide] ul > li:before { clip-path: none; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--accent-color); }
```

- Font sizes: `--secondary-text-size` 28, `--text-size` 40, `--heading-size` 56, `--display-size` 112. Margins: `--frame-padding`, `--frame-top`, `--heading-gap`, `--block-gap`, `--columns-gap`.
- Section covers: `--section-background`, `--section-number-start-color`, `--section-number-end-color`, `--section-texture: none`, `--section-glow-strength: 0%`.
- Progress bar: `--progress-color`, `--progress-color-on-dark`. Soft thesis backgrounds: `--accent-soft-color`, `--second-accent-soft-color`.
- Text colors for dark slides: `--text-color-on-dark`, `--muted-color-on-dark`, `--accent-color-on-dark`.
- One slide of its own: `className` on `Slide` and Tailwind classes in the markup: `className="text-(--accent-color)"`, `className="[--hanging-punctuation:0]"`.
- A dark slide: `background="var(--dark-background)"`; the engine picks the text color.

## Rules of a clear talk

`slidemachina check` checks them. They come from Richard Mayer's principles of multimedia learning and Miller's 7±2 limit of working memory.

| Rule | Limit in `check` |
|---|---|
| A list is short, better 3 to 5 items | at most 7 items |
| Little text on the slide: speech goes to `Notes`, details for the sent copy to `<Slide hidden>` | at most 40 words on a slide, code and notes excluded |
| A diagram is readable in one step | at most 9 boxes and messages without `Focus` |
| Long code goes by steps | over 12 lines only with `lines` |
| At most three columns, numbers or cards in a row | at most 3 columns |
| A talk splits into a few sections | at most 7 top-level sections |
| Every slide has a heading, except a cover, a thesis, a quote and a meme | an `h1` or `h2` |
| Pictures have a description | `alt` on `Image`, `Meme` and `<img>` |
